newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA HEBROSBANK TO CUT CAPITAL TO 10.5 BLN LVS.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA HEBROSBANK TO CUT CAPITAL TO 10.5 BLN LVS.

text.p: Bulgaria's Bank Consolidation Company (BCC), which manages state equity in domestic commercial banks plans to propose a share capital cut in Hebrosbank to 10.5 billion levs, a BCC official said.

"The shareholders will vote whether Hebrosbank's capital be cut to 10.5 billion levs from 15.3 billion after most of its private shareholders rejected to subscribe to a new share issue," BCC executive director Valentin Tzvetanov told Reuters.
The proposal has to be approved on Monday by the BCC's board among other other options, Tzvetanov added.
In July Hebrosbank decided to triple its capital from 763 million levs to 15.3 billion levs through a new share issue open for subcrsiption by October 6.
A new issue of 14.5 billion levs was 67 percent subscribed by the BCC so far, which covered its stake through dollar-denominated domestic bad loans bonds worth of $51 million.

Among biggest bank's private shareholders with around 32 percent are firms, linked to Trade & Savings Bank and Elitbank, which were set under a special supervision by the central bank on September 23.
The BCC, which holds around 67 percent of Hebrosbank's capital, will increase its stake to around 97 percent.
"We have to estimate the bank's capital value in line with BCC's plans to sell off the bank," Tzvetanov said.
South Korean giant Daewoo Corp expressed interest in buying the bank to service its expanding operation in Bulgaria.
